risk_signals.statement: NPL ratio fell from 7.6% (FY2015) to 3.6% (FY2023), ticked up marginally to 3.7% (FY2024), then fell to a series-low 2.5% (FY2025) — City Bank's asset quality did not follow the sector-wide FY2024 deterioration documented elsewhere in this dataset, where median NPL rose from 5.48% to 9.55%. Provision coverage stayed above 100% throughout (110.1% FY2023, 106.8% FY2024, 127.0% FY2025).

ROE rose from 17.6% (FY2023) to a series-high 26.1% (FY2024) and remained strong at 24.4% (FY2025); CAR stayed comfortably above regulatory minimums across the same window (15.8% to 16.0% to 15.7%) — profitability and capital strength continued to move together through the FY2024-2025 period that stressed much of the DSE banking sector.

Reported profit growth in FY2024-2025 masks a sharp change in its source. Net Interest Income fell from 15,831m (FY2023) to 14,490m (FY2024, per the FY2024 report's own contemporaneous figures) to just 2,847m (FY2025) — a 76.4% YoY drop — as the average cost of deposits rose from 3.5% (FY2023) to 4.9% (FY2024) to 5.5% (FY2025), outpacing the rise in yield on advances (8.0% to 9.9% to 10.5%). The bank offset this entirely by more than doubling Investment Income (4,713m FY2023 to 16,615m FY2024 to 35,619m FY2025) as Investments grew from 13.1% to 19.2% to 23.9% of total assets over the same three years. Earnings quality has shifted from core lending spread toward interest-rate-sensitive government-securities income, which is a less durable profit source than the loan-book margin it replaced.

Newly-recovered 2017-2021 interim quarters show City Bank's simple loan-to-deposit ratio (gross loans / customer deposits) running persistently above 100% through its expansion phase -- 101.8% (2017 Q2), 108.9% (2017 Q3), 101.9% (2018 Q2), 105.5% (2018 Q3), 116.7% (2019 Q1), 111.6% (2019 Q2), 106.9% (2019 Q3), 102.3% (2020 Q1), 106.4% (2020 Q2), 105.6% (2021 Q2) -- versus 94-101% in 2012-2016. This is a simple calculated ratio (not the regulatory LDR the bank reports from FY2022 onward on a different basis, e.g. 83.2% for FY2022) but the multi-year direction is consistent with the Tier-II subordinate bond and interbank borrowings lines growing several-fold (from BDT 3.0bn to BDT 9.2bn subordinated debt alone) over the same 2017-2021 window in the underlying quarterly balance sheets -- i.e. loan-book growth during this period was increasingly funded by wholesale borrowing/bonds rather than customer deposits alone.

insights.historical_context: City Bank is now one of the clearest positive outliers in this dataset through the FY2024-2025 Bangladesh banking-sector crisis window: NPL improved (3.6% to 2.5%) while the sector median rose from 5.48% to 9.55%, and ROE improved (17.6% to 24.4%) while several DSE banks recorded provisioning-driven losses or balance-sheet insolvency (NBL, AB Bank) in the same window. This confirms and strengthens the pattern already noted alongside BRAC Bank for 2022-2023. However, the composition of City Bank's FY2024-2025 profit changed materially, shifting toward treasury/government-securities income and away from core net interest income (see earnings_quality_shift signal) — the headline ROE strength is increasingly a treasury-income story. Discrete quarterly cumulative figures also imply Q3 2025 alone had negative net interest income (cumulative-to-Sep 1,455m is below cumulative-to-Jun 1,741m), consistent with the FY2025 annual report's own commentary that funding-cost pressure intensified through the year.

sources.note: City Bank's own Q1 2026 and Half-Yearly 2026 unaudited financial statements PDFs could not be located or downloaded despite an extensive multi-route search: (1) legacy.citybankplc.com/report/financialstatements (this dataset's own source for City Bank's quarterly PDFs through 2021) has not been updated since 2021 and lists nothing for 2022-2026; the site's own nav only links an 'Annual Report' category now, suggesting the quarterly-filing category was deprecated on this CMS, not merely unindexed; (2) the bank's current site (citybankplc.com/reports, discovered via sitemap.xml since it isn't linked from legacy.citybankplc.com) is a client-side-rendered Next.js App Router page -- its server response and every JS chunk fetched were inspected for an embedded data payload or API route and none was found; the site returns HTTP 200 with an empty content shell to both a browser UA and a Googlebot UA; (3) dsebd.org and cse.com.bd company pages both explicitly state 'For detail financial statements, please visit company's website' / point back to the bank's own investor-relation URL, hosting no PDF themselves; (4) Wayback Machine CDX search for citybankplc.com found no capture of any 2025-2026 quarterly-statement PDF or 'city-bank-declares-its-Nth-quarter' press page (a URL pattern that exists for 2021-2022 quarters but was never archived for later years); (5) direct filename guessing against ~15 plausible URL patterns on both legacy.citybankplc.com/files/ and www.citybankplc.com/files/ all returned HTTP 404. What WAS recovered: DSE's own live 'Interim Financial Performance' disclosure table on dsebd.org/displayCompany.php?name=CITYBANK (a primary regulatory disclosure filed directly by the company, independent of the bank's own website) discloses Q1 2026 EPS 1.580, Q2-discrete EPS 1.630, H1-cumulative EPS 3.010, and period-end market prices (29.7, 32.0) -- recorded in quarterly/2026_Q1.json and 2026_Q2.json. DSE's table does not label Solo vs Consolidated; independent press coverage (The Business Standard for Q1: PAT ~Tk241cr, EPS Tk1.6; Prothom Alo/TBS for H1, citing an Aug-2026 earnings-disclosure webcast: CONSOLIDATED H1 PAT Tk526.69cr, CONSOLIDATED EPS Tk3.01, matching DSE's 3.010 almost exactly) suggests the DSE-disclosed EPS may be Consolidated rather than Solo (this dataset's City Bank series is otherwise Solo throughout) -- flagged as an unconfirmed-basis caveat, not resolved. No balance sheet or other income-statement line items were obtainable for either quarter. This should be re-attempted in a future session, ideally with a way to execute the current site's client-side JS or a more targeted search for where the bank now actually publishes its quarterly PDFs.
